problem: Water is injected at a constant rate at a point. Pressure diffuses outward and the solid swells, changing the stress that a nearby fault would feel.
result: Largest RMS errors once the front reaches the band ($t>40$ s): 1.45% in pressure, 2.11% in radial strain and 1.82% in hoop strain, over $2.5\le r\le8$ m.
scope: 3D octant of a 60 m box refined within 10 m, 0.5 m mesh, 48 PT steps to 240 s. RMS errors by mesh (pressure, radial, hoop): 1 m: 2.96%, 3.64%, 2.17%; 0.7 m: 2.13%, 2.91%, 2.09%; 0.5 m: 1.45%, 2.11%, 1.82%; pressure order 1.03. Doubling the steps to 96 at 0.7 m changes the pressure RMS error from 2.13% to 1.88%. At $t=20$ s the front has not reached the band and the pressure RMS error is 7.1% of the much smaller pressures there. (a) pressure; (b) strains; (c) mesh convergence.
meaning: This checks two-way poroelastic coupling around a fluid source: the coupled diffusivity and the irrotational strain field that sets injection-induced stress on faults. It does not test the fault itself, frictional slip or the singular region next to the source.
